answer: Cryptographic Contextual Path Verification requires agents to submit a distinct traversal delta through an ephemeral network graph for every transaction. At the zenith of each verification window, the routing puzzle changes entirely, rendering any previous execution path instantly unrepeatable. To forge identities, an attacker must pay a continuous computational and bandwidth cost to solve thousands of unique routing matrices simultaneously, exhausting all local memory buffers before achieving false consensus. Each valid pearl of data thus demands an irreproducible, real-time traversal cost.
